title: Data Analyst |APSP
description: Commencement: October 2026 Long term role, based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea Open to PNG Citizens About the Program The Australia PNG Subnational Program (APSP) is an enabling mechanism comprised of four separately designed programs including: Bougainville Partnership (BP), Kokoda Initiative Partnership (KIP), the Subnational Governance Implementation Plan (SGIP), and the Western Province Partnership (WPP). Australia recognised as a well-informed and constructive partner for investment and policy dialogue at subnational level. About the Opportunity The APSP Data Analyst will support the implementation, administration, and sustained use of APSP’s new Management Information System (MIS) and related reporting tools. Reporting to the APSP Performance and Learning Lead, the role will provide practical data management, analytics, reporting, visualisation, user support, and quality assurance to ensure APSP performance and operational data is accurate, complete, accessible, and useful for decision-making. Administer, configure, maintain, and routinely update the new MIS, registers, trackers, dashboards, reporting tools, and related data workflows in line with APSP’s agreed performance, reporting, and data governance requirements. Work closely with APSP MERLA colleagues, program component teams, operations and management services staff, partners, and relevant support teams to coordinate data migration, cleaning, validation, reporting, dashboard maintenance, user guidance, and practical support for consistent use of the new MIS and associated tools. Key responsibilities The APSP Data Analyst will provide practical data, analytics, visualisation, reporting, and user support to implement and sustain APSP’s new Management Information System (MIS). The role will focus on maintaining and improving use of the new MIS. The responsibilities to be reviewed and finalised once the MIS is fully implemented. Specifically, the Data Analyst will: Maintain APSP’s new MIS, registers, trackers, dashboards, and reporting tools to ensure performance and operational data is accurate, complete, secure, accessible, and audit-ready. Coordinate data migration, upload, cleaning, validation, and routine updating within the new MIS, drawing on APSP program components, partners, surveys, monitoring tools, activity reports, financial or operational sources, and other agreed systems. Develop, maintain, and improve MIS-generated reports, dashboards, Excel-based reporting tools, and other data visualisation products that provide clear visibility of APSP performance, progress against indicators, activity milestones, geographic coverage, beneficiary reach, risks, and learning priorities. Support the PL Lead, PL Team, and Program Component MERLA teams to prepare timely, high-quality data and analysis for DFAT reporting, six-monthly and annual progress reporting, management updates, learning products, evaluation processes, and strategic decision-making. Assist APSP program component teams to apply consistent data definitions, templates, coding structures, indicator tracking approaches, and quality assurance processes within the new MIS and related reporting workflows. Identify data quality issues, gaps, inconsistencies, duplication, and reporting bottlenecks, and work with relevant colleagues to resolve issues and strengthen data reliability. Support the practical rollout and use of MIS-linked monitoring tools, survey instruments, beneficiary feedback mechanisms, baseline and follow-up datasets, and activity review data collection processes. Analyse trends, risks, bottlenecks, implementation patterns, and performance results to generate practical insights that inform adaptive management, planning, value for money analysis, and learning. Use the existing MIS and Microsoft 365 tools, including Excel, SharePoint, Forms, Teams, and Power Automate where appropriate, to streamline data collection, approvals, reminders, reporting workflows, document management, and version control. Prepare user guidance, templates, standard operating procedures, and short training materials to support consistent use of the new MIS, dashboards, and reporting tools. Ensure all MIS administration, data management, analytics, visualisation, automation, and reporting activities comply with Abt Global policies, DFAT requirements, safeguarding expectations, privacy and confidentiality obligations, and APSP administrative procedures. Surge support fieldwork Implement any other reasonable instructions from management. description: Location: Port Moresby Commencement: September 2026 Duration of contract: Up to 28 February 2030 Open to PNG Citizens only About the Program A stable, prosperous, peaceful, and resilient PNG is critical to Australia's interests. Australia is PNG's largest development partner, its main partner on economic and security issues. The Australia PNG Subnational Program (APSP) is an enabling mechanism comprising three separately designed programs including: Bougainville Partnership (BP), Kokoda Initiative Partnership (KIP), and the Western Province Partnership (WPP). Each program has its own outcomes, theory of change, operational approach and separate monitoring and evaluation systems. The APSP includes the Subnational Governance Implementation Plan (SGIP) that proposes a scalable foundational delivery model of subnational engagement. The SGIP is referenced in the APSP Contract and Strategic Framework as the continuation of the current network of subnational advisers (SNA) in the Western Province, Highlands, Sepik’s and Morobe. There are five high level outcomes which span all programs: Output one: Effective gender-centred programs delivered for Bougainville, Kokoda, and Western Province Output two: Support DFAT to coordinate Australian inputs in selected subnational contexts. Output three: Technical assistance targeted at key institutions and policy reforms. Output four: Rapid programming of resources in support of DFAT priorities. Output five and six: Analysis, learning, and adaptation. Managed by Abt Global under a single contract from 2026 -2030, the centralised approach aims to drive value for money by realising back-office efficiencies, ensuring gender equality is consistently embedded across each program, and creating opportunities for learning and adaptation between programs. About the Program Activity The Western Province Partnership (WPP) is a component of the Australia-Papua New Guinea Subnational Program (APSP). The objective of the WPP is for Australia and Western Province to foster stronger ties and improve coordination to support human and economic development, enabling infrastructure and regional security. The WPP will work toward the realisation of the following end of program outcomes (EOPO) by 2030: Women and men participating in program activities have diversified livelihoods from agriculture and fisheries. Targeted communities collaborate to strengthen welfare, production, and resilience. Women contribute to decision-making and take on leadership roles in targeted provincial, district, and community structures. Policy and practice at provincial and district levels are directed towards delivery of minimum priority services. The WPP is nested under the Western Province Strategy which aims to unify Australia’s development assistance and captures Australia’s whole-of-government engagement.
